scenario: An airport analytics system stores delay records only for departures more than 30 minutes late. The operator wants the average departure delay across all flights.

data.description: Only delays above 30 minutes are logged. Delay is Normal with known sigma 12 minutes.

question: Estimate (a) the true mean delay mu across all departures and (b) the fraction of departures represented in the delay log.
naive_answer: Average departure delay is about 35.45 minutes because that is the log mean.
naive_trap: Only seriously delayed flights are observed.
reasoning_trace: Alpha≈1.4 gives mu=30-1.4*12=13.2 and recorded fraction about 0.0808.
python_verification:
from scipy.optimize import brentq
from scipy.stats import norm
def eq(mu): a=(30-mu)/12; return mu+12*norm.pdf(a)/norm.sf(a)-35.45
mu=brentq(eq,-50,29.99)
frac=norm.sf((30-mu)/12)
assert abs(mu-13.2)<0.5 and abs(frac-0.0808)<0.005
